docs.title: fastapi-jwt
docs.text:
FastAPI native extension, easy and simple JWT auth

Documentation: k4black.github.io/fastapi-jwt Source Code: github.com/k4black/fastapi-jwt

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Report vulnerabilities through GitHub private reporting. See security advisories for affected versions and fixes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• OpenAPI schema generation
  • Native integration with FastAPI
  • Access/Refresh JWT
  • JTI and expiration metadata
  • Optional audience and issuer validation
  • Cookie setting

docs.title: Development and releases
docs.text: Run python -m ruff check fastapi_jwt tests, python -m ruff format --check fastapi_jwt tests, and ty check fastapi_jwt. Release Please manages version and changelog PRs. See the release setup.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
You can access package fastapi-jwt in pypi 

pip install fastapi-jwt[authlib]

python-jose support was removed due to GHSA-3qf3-8w2g-rqmx.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
This library made in fastapi style, so it can be used as standard security features 

from fastapi import FastAPI, Security, Response
from fastapi_jwt import JwtAuthorizationCredentials, JwtAccessBearer


app = FastAPI()
access_security = JwtAccessBearer(secret_key="secret_key", auto_error=True)


@app.post("/auth")
def auth():
    subject = {"username": "username", "role": "user"}
    return {"access_token": access_security.create_access_token(subject=subject)}

@app.post("/auth_cookie")
def auth(response: Response):
    subject = {"username": "username", "role": "user"}
    access_token = access_security.create_access_token(subject=subject)
    access_security.set_access_cookie(response, access_token)
    return {"access_token": access_token}


@app.get("/users/me")
def read_current_user(
    credentials: JwtAuthorizationCredentials = Security(access_security),
):
    return {"username": credentials["username"], "role": credentials["role"]}

For more examples see usage docs

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• FastAPI docs suggest writing it manually, but
  • code duplication

  • opportunity for bugs

  • There is nice fastapi-jwt-auth, but

  • poorly supported
  • not "FastAPI-style" (not native functions parameters)

docs.title: FastAPI Integration
docs.text: FastAPI PR #3305 is closed. FastAPI declined built-in JWT support because token handling belongs in an external package. The maintainer also declined the additional python-jose dependency. See the maintainer response. This project remains a separate FastAPI extension.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or later
  • fastapi >=0.162.2
  • joserfc >=1.8.0,<2.0.0

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Access dependencies reject refresh tokens. Invalid signatures and malformed credential payloads return authentication errors. auto_error=False returns None for invalid credentials. Tokens must contain an object in subject, the expected type, and a finite numeric exp.

Cookie helpers now default to secure=True, httponly=True, and samesite="lax". Use HTTPS. For local HTTP development, pass secure=False explicitly. The keyword-only options preserve positional expires_delta arguments. Use the same cookie options when you unset a cookie. SameSite and HttpOnly do not provide complete CSRF protection. Applications that accept cookies must validate Origin or use CSRF tokens for state-changing requests. Do not change state through GET requests.

The authlib installation extra and AuthlibJWTBackend class now use joserfc. Their public names remain available for compatibility. The implementation does not import deprecated authlib.jose.

docs.title: Contributing to fastapi-jwt
docs.text: First, thanks for taking the time to contribute! 😍 It's highly welcomed, and it can help the project to develop and become more usefully and suitable for everyone.

docs.title: Git Commit Messages
docs.text:
This project uses light version of conventional commits. tl;dr

  • Use the present tense ("Add feature" not "Added feature")
  • Use the imperative mood ("Move cursor to..." not "Moves cursor to...")
  • Limit the first line to 72 characters or less
  • Reference issues and pull requests in commit body
  • When only changing documentation, include [ci skip] in the commit title
  • Consider starting the commit message with an applicable tag:
    • fix - small bug fix
    • docs - docs changes
    • feat - a new feature
    • chore - changes that do not relate to a fix or feature and don't modify src or test files (for example updating dependencies)
    • refactor - code refactor that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
    • style - changes that do not affect the meaning of the code
    • perf - changes that improve performance
    • test - including new or correcting previous tests
    • ci - continuous integration related

For example

Good: * feat: create new api endpoint for student scores reporting * perf: improve performance with lazy load implementation for images * chore: update flask dependency to 2.1 version

Bad: * some fixes * oops * fixed bug on landing page * style changes and update

docs.title: Developing
docs.text:
Use Python 3.11 or later with a virtual environment for development. 

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

Install dev dependencies 

python -m pip install -e ".[docs,test]"

docs.title: Linting and Testing
docs.text:
It is important NOT ONLY to get OK from all linters (or achieve score in the case of pylint), but also to write good code. P.S. It's hard to say what a Good Code is. Let's say that it should be simple, clear, commented, and so on. 

python -m ruff check fastapi_jwt tests
python -m ruff format --check fastapi_jwt tests
ty check fastapi_jwt

Try NOT ONLY to achieve 100% coverage, but also to cover extreme cases, height load cases, multithreaded cases, incorrect input, and so on. 

python -m pytest

You can fix some issues in auto mode.

  • Use Ruff to sort imports and format code. 
    python -m ruff check --fix fastapi_jwt tests
python -m ruff format fastapi_jwt tests

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
Release Please opens a release PR after Conventional Commits reach main. The release PR updates VERSION and CHANGELOG.md. Before version 1.0, breaking changes increase the minor version. For example, 0.3.0 becomes 0.4.0. Merge that PR to create the version tag and GitHub release. The Publish workflow builds the tagged source and uploads both distributions to PyPI. The workflow then publishes the documentation.

Configure these repository secrets before merging the workflow change:

  • RELEASE_APP_ID and RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY: the GitHub App credentials used by k4black/hex.
  • PYPI_TOKEN: the existing PyPI token for this package.

Use the same GitHub App as k4black/hex:

  1. Open GitHub account Settings > Developer settings > GitHub Apps and select that App.
  2. Copy its App ID. Open Install App > Configure for the account and include k4black/fastapi-jwt.
  3. Make sure that the App has Contents: Read and write and Pull requests: Read and write permissions.
  4. Use the original private-key PEM file. If unavailable, generate another key under Private keys without revoking the existing key.
  5. Open k4black/fastapi-jwt > Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > New repository secret.
  6. Add RELEASE_APP_ID with the App ID.
  7. Add RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY with the complete PEM text, including its BEGIN and END lines.

GitHub does not reveal existing secret values. The values cannot be copied from the hex repository through its secret settings. Keep the existing PYPI_TOKEN. No PyPI authentication change is required. The App token lets release PRs trigger CI and GitHub releases trigger publishing. The workflow does not change main or move existing tags.

Breaking changes

  • Require Python 3.11 or later. CI covers Python 3.11 through 3.15.
  • Remove the python-jose backend and extra due to GHSA-3qf3-8w2g-rqmx. Install fastapi-jwt[authlib] instead.
  • Replace deprecated authlib.jose with joserfc. The authlib extra and AuthlibJWTBackend class names remain available.
  • Default cookies to Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax. Use HTTPS, or explicitly set secure=False for local HTTP development.

Authentication fixes

  • Retain the 0.3.1 fixes for refresh-token confusion, invalid signatures, malformed subjects, and from_other(auto_error=False).
  • Validate expiration and token identifiers through the authentication error path.
  • Preserve timedelta(0) in constructors, from_other, token creation, and cookie setters. Token validation retains its 10-second clock leeway.

Features

  • Expose verified expiration through JwtAuthorizationCredentials.exp.
  • Add optional audience and issuer validation. Revocation storage and checks remain application responsibilities.

Maintenance

  • Update FastAPI, development dependencies, documentation dependencies, and GitHub Actions.
  • Adopt Release Please, Ruff lint and format, and ty.
  • Replace the personal email in package metadata with GitHub security reporting links.

Changes: #63, #64, #65, #66, #68.

• Fix refresh-token confusion, invalid signatures, malformed subjects, and explicit optional-authentication overrides.
  • Preserve Python 3.8 support and both JWT backends.
  • Credit @ohgoodjay as the original finder of the access-token type issue in #6.
  • See GHSA-3m23-h9j2-f9xq.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: This library made in fastapi style, so it can be used as standard security features

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
• JwtAuthorizationCredentials - universal credentials for access and refresh tokens. Provide access to subject, unique token identifier (jti), and expiration (exp, Unix seconds). 
    def foo(credentials: JwtAuthorizationCredentials = Security(access_security)):
    return credentials["username"], credentials.jti

docs.title: Access tokens
docs.text:
• JwtAccessBearer - read access token from bearer header only
  • JwtAccessCookie - read access token from cookies only
  • JwtAccessBearerCookie - read access token from both bearer and cookie

docs.title: Refresh tokens
docs.text:
• JwtRefreshBearer - read access token from bearer header only
  • JwtRefreshCookie - read access token from cookies only
  • JwtRefreshBearerCookie - read access token from both bearer and cookie

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
You can create access_security / refresh_security in multiple ways 

# Manually
access_security = JwtAccessBearerCookie(
    secret_key="other_secret_key",
    auto_error=True,
    access_expires_delta=timedelta(hours=1),  # custom access token valid timedelta
    refresh_expires_delta=timedelta(days=1),  # custom access token valid timedelta
)

# Create from another object, copy all params
refresh_security = JwtRefreshBearer.from_other(access_security)

# Create from another object, rewrite some params
other_access_security = JwtAccessCookie.from_other(
    access_security, 
    secret_key='!key!', 
    auto_error=False
)

For tokens, None uses the configured expiration duration, or the duration copied by from_other. timedelta(0) creates a token with exp equal to iat. Token validation retains its 10-second clock leeway. For cookie setters, timedelta(0) sets Max-Age=0 to expire the cookie immediately. Cookie expiration uses only the setter's expires_delta argument, independently of the configured token duration. With None, the setter creates a session cookie without Max-Age.

docs.title: Audience, issuer, and expiration
docs.text:
Set audience or issuer when your application requires those claims. A configured claim must exist and match. Audience validation also accepts a matching entry in a token audience list. The default None does not require a specific audience or issuer.

access_security = JwtAccessBearer(
    secret_key=secret_key,
    audience="my-api",
    issuer="my-auth-service",
)
refresh_security = JwtRefreshBearer.from_other(access_security)

Generated tokens include the configured claims. from_other copies them unless you supply an override. The subject dictionary and credential indexing retain their existing behavior. credentials.exp exposes the verified token expiration in Unix seconds. Applications can use credentials.jti and credentials.exp to store revocations until the token expires. Revocation storage and checks remain application responsibilities.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: This library made in fastapi style, so it can be used as standard security features

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
from datetime import timedelta

from fastapi import FastAPI, Security, HTTPException
from fastapi_jwt import (
    JwtAccessBearerCookie,
    JwtAuthorizationCredentials,
    JwtRefreshBearer,
)


app = FastAPI()


# Read access token from bearer header and cookie (bearer priority)
access_security = JwtAccessBearerCookie(
    secret_key="secret_key",
    auto_error=False,
    access_expires_delta=timedelta(hours=1)  # change access token validation timedelta
)
# Read refresh token from bearer header only
refresh_security = JwtRefreshBearer(
    secret_key="secret_key", 
    auto_error=True  # automatically raise HTTPException: HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED 
)


@app.post("/auth")
def auth():
    # subject (actual payload) is any json-able python dict
    subject = {"username": "username", "role": "user"}

    # Create new access/refresh tokens pair
    access_token = access_security.create_access_token(subject=subject)
    refresh_token = refresh_security.create_refresh_token(subject=subject)

    return {"access_token": access_token, "refresh_token": refresh_token}


@app.post("/refresh")
def refresh(
        credentials: JwtAuthorizationCredentials = Security(refresh_security)
):
    # Update access/refresh tokens pair
    # We can customize expires_delta when creating
    access_token = access_security.create_access_token(subject=credentials.subject)
    refresh_token = refresh_security.create_refresh_token(subject=credentials.subject, expires_delta=timedelta(days=2))

    return {"access_token": access_token, "refresh_token": refresh_token}


@app.get("/users/me")
def read_current_user(
        credentials: JwtAuthorizationCredentials = Security(access_security)
):  
    # auto_error=False, so we should check manually
    if not credentials:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail='my-custom-details')

    # now we can access Credentials object
    return {"username": credentials["username"], "role": credentials["role"]}
